name: Dynamic Light Variation as Sustained Temporal PE Engagement
short_description: Static lighting produces habituation; dynamic light variation (natural or designed) sustains moderate PE engagement and temporal awareness
structural_pattern: Static artificial lighting produces a luminance distribution that is quickly predicted and habituated — within minutes, the visual system has generated an accurate model of the light environment and PE diminishes toward zero. The space becomes perceptually 'dead.' Dynamic light — whether natural (sun movement, cloud passage, seasonal variation) or designed (programmed dimming, responsive controls, daylight integration) — continuously generates new prediction-error events by changing the luminance distribution, CCT, shadow patterns, and intensity on timescales ranging from seconds (cloud shadow) to hours (sun arc) to months (seasonal angle change). This sustained low-to-moderate PE maintains perceptual engagement, reinforces temporal awareness, and prevents the sensory monotony associated with fixed artificial environments.
higher_order_principle: Temporal extension of the Goldilocks zone. As T2 describes the optimal LEVEL of complexity and L1 describes the optimal SPATIAL distribution of luminance PE, L5 describes the optimal RATE OF CHANGE. Too little change (fixed lighting) → habituation, sensory deprivation, loss of engagement. Too much change (flickering, unstable) → distraction, discomfort. Moderate, naturalistic change → sustained engagement in the Goldilocks zone over time. This is the luminous instantiation of the architecture-as-composition thesis: great lighting, like great music, orchestrates PE over time.

temporal_scales.hours: Diurnal arc, CCT shift from morning to evening

causal_links.evidence_base: Natural daylight varies on multiple timescales simultaneously. Each timescale generates PE at a different rate. Static lighting = zero temporal PE. Dynamic lighting = continuous moderate PE.

Moderate sustained PE prevents habituation and maintains cortical engagement. Consistent with the view that one function of moderate environmental complexity is to sustain the brain's active prediction-error processing, preventing DMN-dominance associated with sensory deprivation.

Changing light quality provides implicit time-of-day and weather information. Occupants in daylit spaces report better temporal orientation than those in windowless spaces (Boyce, 2014). Loss of temporal light cues may contribute to the disorientation and malaise of windowless environments.

Flicker (rapid light changes > ~3 Hz) → visual discomfort, migraine trigger. Slow natural variation (minutes-to-hours timescale) → positive engagement. Very slow or absent variation → sensory monotony. The optimal rate of change maps to a temporal Goldilocks zone.

scope_conditions: Applies to all buildings, but effect is most evident in spaces occupied for extended periods (offices, schools, residences, healthcare)
Natural daylight inherently provides dynamic variation; this template is most relevant as a contrast between daylit and artificially-lit spaces
Designed dynamic lighting (tunable CCT/intensity systems, daylight-responsive controls) can partially restore temporal PE in spaces without direct daylight access
The architectural promenade (moving through zones of different light character) is a spatial analog — movement generates light dynamics even if each zone is static
moderators: Occupant mobility: a person who moves through the building encounters light variation spatially even if each zone is static
Task demands: some tasks (surgery, precision assembly) require stable light; dynamic variation would be a liability
Control: occupant-controlled dimming provides agency over the dynamics; automatic changes without user control can be irritating
Rate of change: must be naturalistic (gradual) to be pleasant; abrupt changes are startling

change_rate_goldilocks.optimal: Minutes to hours timescale → positive engagement, sustained alertness
change_rate_goldilocks.too_slow: Static or near-static → sensory monotony, habituation, disengagement

interactions.nature: L1 describes the spatial dimension of luminance PE; L5 describes the temporal dimension. Together they capture the full spatiotemporal PE landscape of architectural light.
T2 = spatial complexity Goldilocks; L5 = temporal complexity Goldilocks for light. Same inverted-U principle, orthogonal dimensions.
Dynamic daylight changes CCT throughout the day (L4 temporal prediction). L5 captures the broader phenomenon of which CCT change is one component.
L5 is Channel 5 of L3. Dynamic variation is one of the six mechanisms through which daylight produces its convergent benefit.

maturity_note: Panel L-II verdict: RETAIN as independent template, upgrade from preliminary to supported-preliminary. Evidence base has grown since L-I but critical 4-hour engagement-decay experiment not yet conducted.

rationale: Evidence base has grown since L-I
Chamilothori's controlled studies provide direct evidence
Residual daylight-preference gap supports independent L5 mechanism
panel_verdict.remaining_limitation: L5 remains the LEAST calibrated of the five light templates

chamilothori_moving_vs_static.finding: Moving sunlight patches preferred over static patches at same contrast

chamilothori_natural_vs_random.finding: Random-dynamic condition rated more interesting than static but LESS pleasant than natural-tracking
chamilothori_natural_vs_random.pe_interpretation: Pattern of dynamics matters — ecological regularity produces higher satisfaction than arbitrary variation
chamilothori_natural_vs_random.implication: L5 is not merely anti-habituation but engages ecological prediction about pattern of light change

dynamic_artificial_lighting_studies.finding: Dynamic artificial lighting produces higher satisfaction than static lighting
dynamic_artificial_lighting_studies.confound: Dynamic systems typically provide circadian optimization (higher melanopic content in morning, lower in evening)
dynamic_artificial_lighting_studies.note: Separating L5 dynamics from L2 circadian optimization not yet achieved

critical_experiment_needed.design: 4-hour engagement-decay: static vs gradual-natural vs gradual-random vs step-change
critical_experiment_needed.measures: Engagement decay functions over sustained occupancy
critical_experiment_needed.status: NOT YET CONDUCTED — required to fully confirm L5 as independent mechanism
critical_experiment_needed.alternative: If experiment fails to show independent dynamics effect, L5 should be absorbed into L3 as one channel
